text:
maya: Heads-up — small-dashboard layout problem: when we render 6+ series the y-axis labels start eating horizontal space. Proposing an "auto-collapse" behavior where we switch to compact unit-only labels at small widths (e.g., `k`, `M`) and show full label on hover. Thoughts?

jamal: +1 on abbrevs. Implementation Q: tooltip on hover for desktop, but what about mobile? Also, need to avoid reflow when toggling.

lucy: UX note: users confuse 'Units' vs 'Metric' — I'd recommend using singular 'Unit' on the axis and an optional hint in the legend: "Unit — requests/sec". Keeps copy consistent across charts.

ava: Accessibility: collapsing visually is fine as long as we expose full text for assistive tech. Don't use `display:none` for SR content. Add `aria-label` on the axis group with the full label and units, e.g., `aria-label="Requests per second (unit: req/s)"`. Also ensure hover tooltips are accessible via keyboard focus.

kai: Smoothing: default on for micro-sparklines (small embeddable charts) but default off for dashboard-level timeseries where anomalies matter. Suggest a per-widget toggle with an indicator in the corner rather than global. We can show a faint overlay that says "Smoothed" when enabled.

maya: Outlier handling question: dim extreme spikes vs inset outliers into a separate mini-axis. Dimming keeps scale intact and preserves context; inset can mislead users about magnitude. Thoughts?

jamal: For runtime: dimming is easier (alpha + stroke) and plays well with streaming. Inset requires additional axis (scale change) and adds complexity to interaction + axis labels. If we do dimming, consider a knee function so we don't dim legitimate peaks that are only slightly above the mean.

lucy: Copy: if we dim outliers we should call the affordance "de-emphasize extreme values" in the chart settings, not "hide outliers". Avoid wording that implies data removal.

maya: Quick mock request: can @kai and @lucy pair on 3 variants — (A) abbrev axis + hover tooltip, (B) collapsed axis with popover on tap/click, (C) full labels and dynamic truncation? We should test with small/mid/large datasets.

kai: I'll do visuals. Putting a Figma link in thread now: https://www.figma.com/file/FAKE/example-axis-variants — includes mobile and desktop frames.

design-bot: New mock uploaded by kai: https://redwood-inference.design/mocks/axis-variants-2026-03-23.png (thumbnail) :frame_with_picture:

ava: A11y checklist items: 1) aria-label on axis group, 2) keyboard-focusable tooltip/popover, 3) ensure color contrast for dimmed spikes (WCAG AA), 4) announce smoothing toggle state with `aria-pressed` or equivalent.

jamal: Implementation snippet idea — toggle collapsed class and rely on CSS for truncation to avoid JS layout churn:

```css
.axis--collapsed {
  max-width: 48px;
  white-space: nowrap;
  overflow: hidden;
  text-overflow: ellipsis;
}
.axis--collapsed abbr[title] {
  border-bottom: 1px dotted; /* visual affordance */
}
```

lucy: UX test plan: recruit 6 PMs/devs, show them A/B/C on a scenario "Identify the anomaly in last 24h" and measure time+accuracy. Also ask screen-reader user to validate aria-label behavior.

maya: Decision for now: prototype A+B+C. Prioritize dimming for outliers and per-widget smoothing toggle (default off for dashboard charts). I'll prototype variations and sync Fri EOD for early feedback.

kai: Noted. Will upload prototypes by Thu afternoon.

maya: Action items:
- kai: produce three mocks + mobile variants (Thu)
- lucy: wording proposals for settings copy (Thu)
- ava: quick a11y smoke test plan (Thu)
- jamal: tech feasibility + perf notes for dimming and collapsed axis (Thu)

maya: Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
